name: Origins of Buddhism
short_desc: A community develops around the Buddha’s teachings on suffering, ethical conduct and liberation in the northern Indian subcontinent.
date_note: A broad origins window reflecting disputed traditional and scholarly dates for the Buddha and early community. These are possible origin bounds, not the duration of Buddhism.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. Adds the religious tradition as a historical development, distinct from the existing Buddha biography and later Asian states. Evidence and date rationale: The sixth-to-fourth-century BCE window is an editorial orientation covering differing traditional and scholarly chronologies for the Buddha and early community. Harvard notes the disputed dates; modern proposals can place the Buddha’s life around 460–380 BCE. These are possible origin bounds, not Buddhism’s duration. The existing Buddha biography retains its separate recorded chronology. Primary evidence: https://pluralism.org/buddhism. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
